hero.headline: TWO ASSISTS FROM ETERNITY.
hero.standfirst: For half an hour, England were headed to MetLife: Anthony Gordon tapped in Morgan Rogers' cross in the 55th and Pickford was repelling everything. Then Messi took over. Enzo Fernández equalised from distance in the 85th, and two minutes into stoppage time Lautaro Martínez headed Messi's cross in at the back post. The champions live on — and Sunday's final is the one the whole tournament pointed to: Spain against Argentina.
hero.photoCaption: Lionel Messi — no goal, both assists. At 39, one game from back-to-back World Cups.

briefing.text: The Crystal Ball called England 2–1; Argentina answered with two goals in the last five minutes plus stoppage. Both semi calls missed — the record drops to 5 from 9.
The early money makes Spain clear final favourites: 42 against Argentina's 27 on Kalshi, with a big 33 on the draw. Half a million dollars traded already.
Rest days today and tomorrow. Saturday: France–England for third place in Miami, 23:00 our time — and the Golden Boot may be settled there. Sunday: the final, 21:00.

facts.text: England led from the 55th to the 85th — five minutes from MetLife when Enzo Fernández struck from outside the box
Messi finished with no goal but both assists, the second a right-footed cross Lautaro headed in at the back post in the 92nd
Pickford denied Álvarez twice and tipped over a González header — a scrappy game with 19 first-half fouls brought only two yellows

yesterday.report: This fixture never does mercy. England played the disciplined, patient game Tuchel promised, and when Morgan Rogers' curling cross found Anthony Gordon at the far post in the 55th, Atlanta's away end believed. Pickford — twice from Álvarez, once from a Nicolás González header — kept the lead alive as Argentina's pressure built and the fouls piled up in a fractious, stop-start contest.
yesterday.report2: Then, as he has for twenty years, Messi decided otherwise. In the 85th he slipped the pass that Enzo Fernández hammered home from range. Two minutes into stoppage time his cross found Lautaro Martínez at the back post, and the header ended it. England's first defeat of the tournament came five minutes from a first final since 1966; the champions march on to face Spain — the final everyone wanted.

star.name: Lionel Messi
star.line: Quiet for eighty minutes, decisive in the ten that mattered: two assists, one final. At 39, he is one win from becoming the first back-to-back champion since Brazil in 1962.

aside.name: Lautaro Martínez
aside.line: The extra-time winner against Switzerland, now the stoppage-time header that broke England. Argentina's closer keeps arriving exactly on time.

today.preview: The game neither wanted, carrying the prize both strikers do: the Golden Boot. Mbappé (8) needs one goal to break his tie with Messi — who plays a day later. Kane (5) and Bellingham (4) get one last swing; so does Dembélé (5). The early market makes France heavy favourites at 50%, with England and the draw level on 26 — heavy legs and heavier hearts after Atlanta.

keyMan.name: Kylian Mbappé
keyMan.line: Blanked by Spain, stuck on 8, and handed one more game. A goal in Miami and the Golden Boot is effectively his — unless Messi answers at MetLife on Sunday.

today.venue: MetLife Stadium, New York / New Jersey
today.preview: The two best teams of the tournament, and it isn't close: Spain's record wall against the champions who refuse to die. Spain have conceded twice all tournament; Argentina have won their last three knockouts after trailing or level in the closing stages. Yamal against Messi — the heir against the throne. The early money leans Spanish: 42 to 27, with a third of it on the draw. The Crystal Ball returns Sunday morning with the full call.
watch: Yamal v Messi — the 18-year-old face of the next decade against the 39-year-old face of the last two

keyMan.name: Lamine Yamal
keyMan.line: A penalty won against France, a semi-final owned, and now the stage every 18-year-old dreams of. Beat Argentina and the torch isn't passed — it's taken.
